title: Patsy Cline's birth chart
metaDescription: Patsy Cline's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.8° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a square: Mars and Uranus within 0.2°, drive wired to disruption. A square is friction that produces motion — the aspect the tradition credits with building capability precisely by refusing to be comfortable.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 15.8° Virgo: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Saturn. A earth sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 29.0° Leo; Mars stands at 22.5° Cancer. The tradition reads a mind that decides at speaking speed from Mercury, drive that moves on certainty and current from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mars and Uranus: 0.2° from an exact square. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, Uranus square Pluto at 0.3°, and Mars conjunction Pluto at 0.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars opposes Saturn while both square Uranus. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. Mars in Cancer at 22.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Virgo at 6.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Capricorn at 28.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in earth, 2 in fire, 2 in water by element, 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 1 fixed by modality. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Venus crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day, so its sign is left open. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.8° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
